scalars.scalar_value: Associates degree or higher in related law enforcement field or customer service

A District on-line application on http://hr.fhda.edu/careers/. *In the application, you will provide information, which demonstrates your understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff. Additionally, you will be asked to explain how your life experiences, studies or work have influenced your commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be completion of the twelfth (12th) grade or equivalent supplemented by college-level.

items.item_text: Perform basic first aid and CPR procedures
Possession of, or ability to obtain, a valid California Driver’s License by time of appointment.
Obtain a POST certificate in Traffic 101A and to legally write police reports and non-injury traffic accidents within one year of employment.
Obtain and maintain American Red Cross First Aid and CPR certification.
Associates degree or higher in related law enforcement field or customer service

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be completion of the twelfth (12th) grade or equivalent supplemented by college-level.

A current resume of all work experience, formal education and training.
English grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation
Provide high-level customer service and foster positive working relationships with students, staff, faculty, and the public
Familiarity of structure of Federal and California State Laws
Common safety practices and principles
Obtain critical information from individuals in stressful or emergency situations
A cover letter addressing your qualifications for the position.
Accurately observe, recall, and detail faces, names, physical characteristics, locations, and incident facts
Conduct basic interviews and investigations regarding crimes, traffic, and related campus incidents
Analyze situations accurately, identify core problems, evaluate options, and recommend or implement effective courses of action
Prepare clear, comprehensive, and concise incident reports and documentation
Use tact, discretion, confidentiality, and independent judgment within established scope of authority, policies, and legal guidelines
Organize tasks, set priorities, meet deadlines, and handle detailed office support work efficiently
Basic Computer skills
Communicate clearly, effectively, and professionally in English (oral and written), including over the phone and via radio equipment

Organizational skills
